Core development means working on the core RASENMAEHER API (rmapi) — the service that owns user CRUD and Deploy App operations and that every product integration registers with over mTLS. If you want to add a new service to Deploy App, you are building a product integration API instead; see Build an Integration. This page is for changing the core itself.

Who this is for

You are in the right place if you are:

  • Fixing or extending the core API: user lifecycle, enrollment, certificate issuance flows, the callback contract that drives product integrations.
  • Working on the UI that talks to the core, or on the deployment plumbing that ships it.
  • Debugging how the core behaves end-to-end across the whole stack.

If instead you are wiring a product (Matrix, TAK, MediaMTX, or your own) into Deploy App, you do not modify the core — you build a product integration API against its contract. Start from pvarki/python-integration-template and read Build an Integration.

The repo map

The core lives in one repository; the surrounding stack aggregates it.

Repo Role
pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api The core **rmapi**. The rasenmaeher_api Python package; the rmapi service/container. This is where core changes happen.
pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration Legacy stack (Docker Compose). Aggregates the core and all other components as git submodules; api/ is the submodule pointing at python-rasenmaeher-api.
pvarki/opendefence-platform New stack (Kubernetes, alpha). Runs the core as deployment/opendefense-rmapi in namespace opendefense-system.
pvarki/python-integration-template Copier scaffold for building a product integration API (not the core).

In the legacy stack the components are git submodules. From the compose repo's README.rst, the relevant ones include:

  • api → pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api (the core)
  • miniwerk → pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-miniwerk (Let's Encrypt certs, subdomains)
  • cfssl → pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-cfssl (the internal CA)
  • uiv2 → pvarki/react-rasenmaeher-ui-v2 (the UI)
  • plus product integrations such as takintegration, battlelog, mtxauthz

Note: Because components are submodules, changes to the core are made inside the api/ submodule on its own branch and pushed to python-rasenmaeher-api, not committed against the aggregate repo. See the compose README.rst section "Git submodules".

The contribution loop

  1. Set up a dev environment for your target stack. The two stacks are genuinely different to develop against:
    • Legacy → Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose)
    • Kubernetes → Set up your dev environment (Kubernetes)
  2. Run the inner loop. Edit the core, hot-reload, exercise it:
    • Legacy → Iterate on the core API (Docker Compose)
    • Kubernetes → Iterate on the core API (mirrord)
  3. Understand the surface you are changing. See Core APIs & the rmapi contract for what the core exposes and the mTLS callback contract product integrations depend on — breaking it breaks every integration.
  4. Test and pass the gates. See Testing & CI conventions.
  5. Open a PR following org conventions. Branch naming, commit style, linting, and CI library are documented on the Community & Standards page in the Contribute to Project book, which links pvarki/markdown-pvarki-best_practises and pvarki/config-ci-library.

Where to go next

  • New to the project as a whole? Read the Introduction book first.
  • Running a deployment rather than developing it? See the Operate book.
  • Contributing process, code style, and community rules live in Contribute to Project.
